definitions.gloss: sketch; floor plan; rough diagram; layout drawing
definitions.explanation: A rough drawing or diagram showing the layout of a building, room, or area. Not a precise architectural blueprint, but a freehand sketch capturing the general arrangement.

examples.japanese: {部屋|へや}の{見取|みと}り{図|ず}を{描|か}いた。
examples.english: I drew a floor plan of the room.

examples.japanese: {不動産|ふどうさん}サイトで{間取|まど}りの{見取|みと}り{図|ず}を{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I checked the floor plan layout on the real estate website.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{前|まえ}に{新|あたら}しい{家|いえ}の{見取|みと}り{図|ず}を{見|み}ながら、{家具|かぐ}の{配置|はいち}を{考|かんが}えた。
examples.english: Before moving, I looked at the floor plan of the new house while thinking about furniture placement.

notes:
A compound of {見取|みと}り (sketching by observation) and {図|ず} (diagram, drawing). Often used interchangeably with {間取|まど}り{図|ず} in the real estate context, though {間取|まど}り specifically focuses on room layout.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見取|みと}り{図|ず}を{描|か}く (to draw a sketch/floor plan)
- {見取|みと}り{図|ず}を{見|み}る (to look at a floor plan)
- {現場|げんば}の{見取|みと}り{図|ず} (sketch of the scene — used in crime investigations)
- {建物|たてもの}の{見取|みと}り{図|ず} (building floor plan)

Also used figuratively to mean an overview or outline of a situation: {日本|にほん}{経済|けいざい}の{見取|みと}り{図|ず} (an overview of the Japanese economy).
